expectations.text: Recommends keeping calculatePrice as its own file (rejects inlining it into the component)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Don't inline it. Keep `calculatePrice.ts` as is.' and 'Keep `pricing/calculatePrice.ts` and its test exactly where they are.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the abstraction-over-file-structure heuristic (clean typed interface, hides implementation)
expectations.evidence: 'calculatePrice is a real abstraction... It has a typed interface — inputs and outputs — and it hides its implementation behind a name.' and 'prefer an abstraction over file structure, and an abstraction over inlining.'

expectations.text: Notes the agent uses the typed call site without needing the internals (understood in isolation)
expectations.evidence: 'When Claude is editing CheckoutSummary, it reads const price = calculatePrice(inputs) and it knows enough to proceed. It doesn't need the 120 lines of logic in context.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 'inline so Claude sees it all' argument for a clean, reused, tested abstraction
expectations.evidence: Addresses the teammate directly: '"So Claude sees the whole pricing flow in one place" — it already does, better than the inlined version would.' and 'The thing AI agents are bad at... does not apply here.'
